skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest X-ray for a suspected radiopaque foreign body and determining its precise anatomical location relative to the hila.
steps: Scan the lung fields and mediastinum for distinct radiopaque densities that differ from normal vascular or bony structures.
Project the density onto the hilar regions (right vs. left) by tracing the bronchovascular markings and comparing symmetry with the contralateral side.
Distinguish the correct hilum by verifying if the opacity aligns with the expected course of the main or lobar bronchi, ruling out superimposed rib or vessel artifacts.

skills.trigger: When correlating endoscopic findings of an airway foreign body with the absence of typical obstructive symptoms (atelectasis or air trapping) on imaging.
steps: Inspect the endoscopic view specifically for the morphology of the foreign body, looking for a central opening or tubular structure.
Assess whether the object allows for a patent lumen through which air can pass, rather than causing a complete seal against the bronchial wall.
Conclude that the presence of a patent lumen explains the lack of downstream collapse (atelectasis) or hyperinflation (air trapping), distinguishing it from solid obstructing objects.
